page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the first-generation N1 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU, or 0.9 GB per core. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud hardware. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, while the multi-core score reaches 1408.88. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 13.22 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.3 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also limited, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 652.65 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 18.91 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources, though it trades off memory capacity and raw performance. It is suited for lightweight, CPU-focused tasks with minimal memory footprints, such as basic static web serving, simple Redis key-value operations, or small-scale background processing.

Lacking integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance provides a dedicated CPU allocation with a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB. Benchmark results place its processing and memory capabilities in the lower performance tiers, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1408.88 and a Passmark memory score of 730.43. The instance is qualitatively cost-effective for lightweight, compute-bound workloads that do not require substantial memory, such as basic static web serving, simple Redis operations, or low-intensity background tasks.
